tips.greetings: 💡 Add krap (men) or ka (women) to the end of any phrase to make it polite.
tips.food: 💡 "Mai phet" = not spicy. "Phet nit noi" = a little spicy. Street food is safe and delicious — go where locals eat.
tips.directions: 💡 Agree on a tuk-tuk price before getting in. Bangkok's BTS Skytrain and MRT are far easier — signs are in English.
tips.numbers: 💡 Prices are almost always shown in Arabic numerals. Focus on learning the spoken words.
tips.shopping: Night markets expect bargaining. Mall prices are fixed.
tips.medical: Call 1669 for an ambulance. Private hospitals in Bangkok are used to travelers.
tips.immigration: Have an onward ticket and a hotel address. The tourist police line is 1155.
tips.hotel: Shoes come off at temple stays and many guesthouses. Ask whether tax is included.
tips.transport: Grab works in the cities. On the BTS or MRT, a stored-value card is worth it.

pronGuide.title: Thai Sounds
tips: Thai has 5 tones — for tourists, a flat (mid) tone works for most common words
Rising tone for yes/no questions sounds more natural
Avoid strong falling tones on greetings — it can sound impatient
Double consonants like "kk" represent a brief stop before the sound

culture.rule: The wai is the standard greeting
culture.note: Press your palms together at chest level and bow slightly. Return a wai when someone offers one to you.
Lèse-majesté laws are strictly enforced. Any criticism of the royal family is illegal and taken very seriously.

culture.rule: Feet are considered low and unclean
culture.note: Never point your feet at people, sacred images, or monks. Don't prop your feet on tables or chairs.
The head is considered the most sacred part of the body. Even patting a child on the head is inappropriate.
Shoulders and knees must be covered. Many temples provide wraps at the entrance for a small fee.
Female travellers should not hand anything directly to a monk or make physical contact.

money.note: Street food, tuk-tuks, and local markets are cash only. Keep ฿500–1,000 on you at all times.
That's about $6 — take out more at once rather than multiple small withdrawals. Kasikorn Bank is reliable.

money.rule: Super Rich money changers give the best rates
money.note: Look for 'Super Rich' exchange booths in Bangkok — consistently better than banks or airport counters.
Chatuchak Weekend Market and street stalls — start at 50–60% of the asking price. Smile and be friendly.
฿20–50 for good restaurant service, ฿100 for a massage. Round up taxi fares.

food.name: Pad Thai
food.what: Stir-fried rice noodles with egg, tofu or shrimp, bean sprouts, and crushed peanuts
food.tip: Always customise with the condiment tray: fish sauce, chilli, sugar, and vinegar.

food.name: Tom yum goong
food.what: Spicy lemongrass and lime prawn soup — intensely aromatic and sour
food.tip: Ask for 'mai phet' (not spicy) if needed. The galangal and lemongrass are not meant to be eaten.

food.name: Mango sticky rice
food.what: Sweet glutinous rice soaked in coconut milk served with fresh mango slices
food.tip: Best in mango season (March–June). A must-try dessert.

food.name: Som tam
food.what: Green papaya salad pounded with chilli, lime, fish sauce, tomatoes, and dried shrimp
food.tip: Specify your spice level upfront — even 'medium' can be very hot by Western standards.

food.name: Massaman curry
food.what: Mild, rich coconut curry with potato and peanuts — Persian-influenced and fragrant
food.tip: Less common than green curry but arguably more complex. Best with beef or lamb.

food.name: Street food safety
food.what: Eat where locals eat — high turnover means fresh food, even from roadside stalls
food.tip: If it smells amazing and has a queue, it's good. Cooked-to-order is always safer than pre-made.

safety.note: A friendly local tells you about a 'once-in-a-lifetime' sale on rubies or sapphires you can resell for profit. 100% a scam — the gems are worthless.
Driver offers a very cheap tour, then takes you to shops where he gets a commission. Politely decline and use Grab instead.
'That temple is closed today — I'll take you to a special one.' It's never closed. Always verify yourself before changing plans.
Tourist police speak English and are specifically trained to help foreigners. Save this number.
Wat Phra Kaew (Grand Palace) enforces strict rules — no sleeveless tops or shorts. Wraps are available to rent at the entrance.
